description: Team CISS is a passionate multidisciplinary group of developers, systems thinkers, and space science enthusiasts who build Space Mission Systems Architect: Interplanetary Systems Engineering & Trade-Off Simulation, successfully bridging the gap between educational science communication and interactive web gaming. For this project, the team designed an immersive web-based simulation where players balance real-world mission constraints such as tight budgets, strict payload mass limits, radiation shielding, power generation, and communication throughput. Developed entirely from scratch, the simulation features core game mechanics and trajectory calculations, including gravity assist trade-offs, built using JavaScript and HTML5 alongside a responsive sci-fi mission control cockpit interface complete with live telemetry streaming. Through this project, Team CISS demonstrates how open data, creative web development, and aerospace education can come together to inspire the next generation of space systems architects and explorers.
summary:
Space Mission Systems Architect is an interactive, web-based space mission simulation built by the Ceylon Institute of Space Science (CISS). It is composed of a 3D WebGL spacecraft hangar, real-time orbital trajectory visualization, GMAT-inspired astrodynamics, solo and four-role cooperative multiplayer modes, and many more exciting features.
This was made for aspiring aerospace engineers and students who often don't get to experience how spacecraft subsystems interact under strict real-world constraints. Our simulation allows players to experience challenges such as balancing payload mass limits, budget caps, deep-space power decay, radiation shielding, communication bandwidth, and mid-flight anomalies. The space mission targets in our simulation include Europa, Titan, and 16 Psyche, and each of them has a unique quest to be completed.
This simulation also allows competitive contract scenarios and an unrestricted physics sandbox. In four-player team mode, the responsibilities are divided among the participants into distinct crew roles such as Commander, Lead Engineer, Chief Scientist, and Flight Director.
By transforming complex orbital mechanics and spacecraft engineering into an accessible simulation, we were able to bridge the gap between theoretical physics and real-world engineering trade-offs. This allows us to equip the next generation of explorers with the collaborative and analytical skills required for future interplanetary missions.
details:
Space Mission Systems Architect Simulation Game

Space Mission Systems Architect is an interactive, web-based spacecraft engineering and mission simulation platform. It works by allowing players (either solo or in a team of up to four) to design, configure, launch, and manage a complete space mission from concept to orbit.

The players first define a mission objective by selecting one of the 3 destinations provided (Europa, Titan, or 16 Psyche) and a difficulty tier (Cadet- easy, Commander- medium, and Architect- hard).

Europa and Titan were chosen because, even though both are outer-system moons, the Europa mission requires deep-space radiation shielding against intense Jovian plasma belts, whereas the Titan mission requires navigating a dense organic nitrogen atmosphere and cryogenic hydrocarbon environments. 16 Psyche presents an entirely different asteroid-belt challenge centered on mapping a metallic, core-origin body and dealing with magnetic anomalies rather than planetary gas or ice layers.

How does it work?

The game begins by asking players to choose between a solo mission or a cooperative multiplayer team session, which can support up to four players. If team mode is selected, the roles can be divided as Commander, Lead Engineer, Chief Scientist, and Flight Director. Some other features that are available include a head-to-head competitive scenario between 2 teams and an unrestricted physics sandbox.

Once a mode and a mission objective are selected, players are then subjected to a spacecraft configuration workflow. Here, managing budget credits, payload mass caps, and selecting subsystem assemblies (such as selecting power systems like solar arrays or nuclear RTGs, communications antennas, and scientific instruments) are done while ensuring compatibility with the chosen launch vehicle and trajectory play (Direct or Gravity Assist).

Every customization of the spacecraft dynamically updates an interactive Three.js 3D WebGL hangar model in real time. Once launched, a real-time telemetry dashboard tracks progress, power draw, fuel consumption, and communications throughput along an interactive orbital visualizer. During transit, a random, destination-specific mid-flight anomaly triggers alerts that require immediate engineering decisions before the simulation concludes. The game concludes with a diagnostic post-mission report that evaluates success or failure, efficiency, and scientific yield. All completed missions are automatically archived to storage for side-by-side comparisons, and if the player requires it, their mission can be included in the Hall of Fame ranking.

What benefits does it have?

It bridges theory and practice by transforming abstract physics and aerospace formulas into practical, visual trade-offs. This shows players how a choice in one area impacts another during real-world scenarios.

Multiplayer mode allows the division of responsibility across four distinct crew roles, which fosters active teamwork and negotiation.

It allows players to learn from their mistakes by including diagnostic debriefs that help to improve their performance.

This game has been made in a way that allows players to learn the concepts while interacting with the features present.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our intention was to provide hands-on aerospace education and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space enthusiasts world-wide. Our game provides an engaging environment where students can safely experiment, make mistakes, and learn from integrated mission design without expensive hardware or physical constraints. This builds vital problem-solving, systems-thinking, and collaborative skills necessary for future space explorations.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

The coding languages that were used include HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+).

Some libraries and frameworks that were used include Three.js (for the 3D WebGL spacecraft hangar inspection engine), JSZip (for automated local extraction of country flag assets), and Firebase Realtime Database / JSONBin.io (for cross-device multiplayer room synchronization and global mission archiving).

Software and infrastructure that were used included Browser-based development environments, Git/GitHub for version control, and standard web hosting platforms.

How is your project creative?

Our game introduces creative mechanics that elevate it far beyond a standard static quiz or calculator. Every subsystem selection is dynamically built, and it updates a real-time 3D WebGL spacecraft in the hangar and renders custom vector graphics during flight transit. There are destination-specific anomaly events that force players to make real-time operational compromises mid-flight.

It also contains a Mission Viz Interplanetary Trajectory Map. It dynamically represents scaled orbital paths for the destinations (Europa, Titan, and 16 Psyche). This provides players with immediate spatial feedback on their interplanetary navigation.

The game also incorporates a moving cosmic background and authentic mission-control audio design, including ambient space soundscapes and mechanical button telemetry clicks that evoke an authentic mission control atmosphere. Every mission also concludes with a unique video tailored to whether your spacecraft successfully unlocked the secrets of Europa's icy crust, survived Titan's dense methane haze, or mapped 16 Psyche's metallic core, and dramatic failure logs if the mission fails.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team wanted the experience to be intuitive and educational for learners of all backgrounds. We focused heavily on accessibility and usability through clear visual hierarchies, color-coded status badges, and immersive audio feedback. This game was made to be an educational adventure that gently introduces complex aerospace concepts.
